fields.title: DICTO 1:2 Truncated Octahedron: The 4D Vacuus of the Permutohedron
fields.abstract: The 4D permutohedron is the skeleton of the web of all orderings of 1 to 5 (120 orders, 240 exchanges of neighbouring values). Its 4D Vacuus is the set of 3D slices through its centre that between them carry all of its 2-faces, as DICTO's 3D Vacuus solids are built from central planes carrying all their edges. Theorem 1: the 150 two-dimensional faces lie in exactly 65 central slices, in four congruence classes (30, 20, 10, 5), each described exactly. Theorem 2: the five slices that hold the middle value fixed are the DICTO 1:2 Truncated Octahedron (the permutohedron of 1, 2, 4, 5: squares of side 1, hexagons with sides 1 and 2 in turn), and any two cross in a regular hexagon through the centre. Theorem 2b: for 2m+1 values, where k of the central slices p_i = m+1 cross, the section is the permutohedron of explicit values (k odd: the middle k values taken out; k even: the middle k+1 taken out and the middle value put back), down to a regular hexagon in every odd dimension; Lemma 2a gives the section of any permutohedron by one coordinate held fixed. Theorem 3: the number of central hyperplanes through the ridges of the permutohedron of 1..n is 3, 15, 65, 225, 770, 2443, 7761 for dimensions 2 to 8, with a closed formula. Theorem 4: the semi-uniform truncated octahedra T(x) of DICTONIC's golden bond are the permutohedra of four values placed symmetrically about zero. A search found no earlier construction of a 4D solid from central slices carrying all its 2-faces.
fields.ai_statement: The idea of the 4D Vacuus (a 4D solid built from central 3D slices carrying all its 2-faces), the shapes studied and all names are DICTO's. Claude computed the slices exactly, found and proved Theorems 1 to 4, Lemma 2a and Theorem 2b, searched the prior art and drafted the text. DICTO read and approved the typeset paper before release on Zenodo. No outside referee has checked the proofs, and they are not formally verified.
fields.process_summary:
1. 10 Nov 2026: DICTO asked for the 4D Vacuus of the permutohedron. Claude computed the central hyperplanes of all 150 2-faces (first in floating point, then exactly in rational arithmetic) and classified the slices up to symmetry.
2. 11 Nov: exact classes (four, not the floating-point eight); the crossing of the five central slices (regular hexagons); the count N(n) by brute force for n = 3..9 and its closed formula; the link to DICTONIC's T(x). Version 1 released after review by an in-house panel of automated referees and one independent attack (reports and judgements kept with the paper's data); Versions 2 and 3 added figures, references and history.
3. 12 Nov: Version 4. Lemma 2a and Theorem 2b (the heart in every odd dimension), checked exactly for 3 to 21 values; the figure of the hearts for 5 to 21 values; a prior-art search for earlier 4D Vacuus forms (library and web; none found).
fields.verification_notes: Exact rational arithmetic throughout (Python fractions, gmpy2): every 2-face's central hyperplane, every slice's faces (plane plus all corners strictly on one side), Euler characteristic 2 (vacuus4d_exact.py). N(n) by brute force over every ridge for n = 3..9, against the closed formula (vacuus_general.py). Crossings: crossing5.py (exact); Theorem 2b by majorization and LP support functions for n = 3..9 (heart_every_dim.py) and by the Birkhoff (doubly stochastic) form for n = 15..21 (heart_check_big.py); a deliberately wrong value set is rejected each time. Every script ends with a FINAL ok/FAIL line. Human reading: DICTO read the typeset paper. No outside referee; no formal proof. Data, scripts and checks at the exact commit: https://github.com/DICTOR-Master/kaleidohedra/tree/ab31fb48/studies/2026-11-10-permutohedron
fields.negative_results: A first floating-point classification split one slice class into several types by rounding; superseded by the exact computation. A first closed formula for N(n) failed for even n (two splits give the same hyperplane) and was corrected and rechecked. In the Theorem 2b check, three intended negative controls were not negatives (every coordinate section of a permutohedron is again a permutohedron), so the control was replaced by rejecting wrong value sets. Several automated-referee objections were rejected because exact checks contradicted them (judgement kept in the paper's folder).
